title: Vaupel (2010): Multiple Choice
instructions: Choose the single answer most accurately supported by the reading.

items.prompt: Which statement best captures the review's central conclusion?
options: The biological aging rate in humans had already been reduced by more than half
Mortality and senescence shifted later as people reached old age healthier
Illness and disability had disappeared in every country and older age group
A single longevity gene explains most recent gains independently of living conditions
items.answer: Mortality and senescence shifted later as people reached old age healthier
items.explanation: Vaupel emphasizes postponed mortality associated with better health rather than an established historical reduction in the slope of deterioration.

items.prompt: What do X5 and X10 in Figure 1 represent?
options: Ages at which annual death probabilities reach exactly 5% and 10%
Dates when life expectancy at birth increased by five and ten years
Ages with five and ten years of remaining life expectancy
Countries with fivefold and tenfold probabilities of reaching 100
items.answer: Ages with five and ten years of remaining life expectancy
items.explanation: The upward movement and relatively stable gap between these threshold ages support the argument for postponement.

items.prompt: What can be read directly from Figure 2?
options: Rapid growth in Swedish women aged 100+ and Japanese women aged 105+
Universal survival without disability or chronic illness at the oldest ages in both countries
Complete disappearance of disability among supercentenarians
Equal mortality rates for women and men
items.answer: Rapid growth in Swedish women aged 100+ and Japanese women aged 105+
items.explanation: The figure charts numbers of very old women, not each individual's health or a biological maximum lifespan.

items.prompt: Why is evidence for delayed debility less clear than evidence for delayed death?
options: Deaths are never recorded in population statistics
Health measurement becomes uniformly reliable after age 85
All countries use identical disability measures and participation rules
Health measurement and selective participation complicate comparisons
items.answer: Health measurement and selective participation complicate comparisons
items.explanation: The review notes limited and mixed evidence, particularly after age 85 and for cognition, as well as survey participation problems among people in poor health.

items.prompt: Which three broad health states does Vaupel distinguish?
options: Perfect health, functional limitation, and death
Genes, environment, and behavior
Youth, middle age, and old age
Healthy, unhealthy, and dead
items.explanation: The unhealthy state is then divided into chronic illness with functioning and disability, separating morbidity from loss of function.

items.prompt: How can effective rehabilitation change health outcomes?
options: It must eliminate both the disease diagnosis and every functional limitation
It can reduce disability without reducing morbidity
It improves measured disability only by increasing the death rate
It makes the diagnosis itself cease to exist
items.answer: It can reduce disability without reducing morbidity
items.explanation: A person may retain an illness while functioning better with a pacemaker or physical therapy. Morbidity and disability need not move together.

items.prompt: Which statement describes the health–survival paradox?
options: Men may appear healthier yet die younger than women
Women are healthier at every age but also die earlier than men
There are no measurable differences in either health or survival between women and men
Older men invariably make more routine medical visits than women
items.answer: Men may appear healthier yet die younger than women
items.explanation: Possible explanations include health perceptions, care use, risk behavior, and survival in poor health; the review does not establish their relative contributions.

items.prompt: Why can population mortality flatten in the left-hand model of Box 1?
options: Every individual's mortality risk eventually becomes zero
All subpopulations acquire a negative rate of aging
Selective survival changes the mix of subpopulations
Missing birth records make validated age comparisons impossible
items.answer: Selective survival changes the mix of subpopulations
items.explanation: Higher-mortality subpopulations diminish first. Their changing representation can flatten the aggregate curve while mortality rises within each subpopulation.

items.prompt: How does the review assess genetic explanations of lifespan?
options: Modest overall influence, potentially greater at the oldest ages
One identified gene determines most lifespan variation regardless of education and medical care
Genetic variation plays no role at any age
APOE multiplies death risk tenfold in every population
items.answer: Modest overall influence, potentially greater at the oldest ages
items.explanation: This preserves both the approximately 25% twin-study estimate and the qualification that genetic influence might be more important at the very oldest ages.

items.prompt: Which two contributors to postponed senescence interact, leaving their relative importance uncertain?
options: Prosperity and medicine
Birth month and astrological sign
Immigration and fertility
Genes and maximum lifespan
items.explanation: Prosperity supports treatment, education, and research, while better health supports productivity and prosperity.

items.prompt: Which distinction between behavior and population longevity matches Vaupel's argument?
options: Individual diet, exercise, and smoking have no bearing on longevity relative to contemporaries
Personal behavior alone fully explains every national difference and historical increase
Behavior matters for relative longevity; prosperity and medicine shape population levels
Population longevity is independent of social conditions and fixed solely by parental lifespan
items.answer: Behavior matters for relative longevity; prosperity and medicine shape population levels
items.explanation: The article recognizes behavioral influences while distinguishing them from the broader conditions shaping a population's general longevity level.

items.prompt: How should the projection of children reaching age 100 be interpreted?
options: A guaranteed forecast for every individual child
A conditional extrapolation of continued mortality improvement
A definite outcome already observed through genetic testing
An outcome already produced by the work-hour scenario in Figure 4
items.answer: A conditional extrapolation of continued mortality improvement
items.explanation: The statement depends on a continued historical pace of mortality reduction, and that continuation is explicitly debated.

items.prompt: Which pair correctly describes the Swedish female counterfactuals after age 50?
options: Halving death probabilities gives age 118; halving the aging rate gives age 90
Both changes leave the expected age at death at 84
Halving death probabilities gives age 90; halving the aging rate gives age 118
Both changes give an expected age at death of exactly 100
items.answer: Halving death probabilities gives age 90; halving the aging rate gives age 118
items.explanation: Using an expected age at death of 84 as the baseline, the two calculations illustrate the difference between mortality levels and the rate of aging.

items.prompt: What redistribution of work does Figure 4 illustrate?
options: Longer weekly hours only in youth, followed by mandatory retirement for everyone at 50
Exactly the same 40-hour working week at every age without variation or exceptions
A ban on employment at older ages
Work across more years with reduced weekly hours earlier in life
items.answer: Work across more years with reduced weekly hours earlier in life
items.explanation: The hypothetical scenario reallocates effort across ages to preserve output while changing the mix of work, education, family life, and leisure.

items.prompt: What is the central question of the longevity riddle?
options: Why human beings have no genes involved in survival
Why mortality levels have shifted while aging rates appear stable
Why every country has exactly the same life expectancy at birth
Why unverified reports of extreme ages are sufficient to establish individual aging mechanisms
items.answer: Why mortality levels have shifted while aging rates appear stable
items.explanation: Vaupel presents a similar or possibly invariant rate of mortality increase as a hypothesis to investigate, not a settled biological law.
